note: Outside the test set: a hand-written sketch from the worksheet (screen, limit, offer, reward, cap, decline and failure paths are Aadi's; the rest is filled in).

candidate.title: Out of lives? One life now for a short game
candidate.what_is_different_here: A player gets up to 5 lives, a failed level costs 1, and one comes back every 30 minutes (s01.e01, s02.e02). The out-of-lives pop-up (s02) sells more lives for gold bars (s02.e03), which cost real money.
candidate.trigger_event: The player taps Play on a level with 0 lives, which opens the out-of-lives pop-up
candidate.placement: A button under the gold-bar button in the out-of-lives pop-up
candidate.offer_copy: Out of lives? Play a short game to get 1 life now.
candidate.frequency_cap: Up to 3 a day, resets at midnight local time
candidate.decline_path: Closing it changes nothing: the pop-up and the life timer work as today.
candidate.ad_fail_path: If no game is ready, the button is hidden. If the game doesn't count, no life is given and the try isn't used.
candidate.subscriber_treatment: There is no subscription; every player sees the same offer.

flow_steps.caption: The player taps Play on a level with 0 lives.
The out-of-lives pop-up shows the new button under the gold-bar button.
The player plays a short game and can close it at any time.
The heart meter shows 1 life and the level can start.

candidate.after_reward: When the life is used, lives come back every 30 minutes as today, and the button offers another life, up to 3 a day.
candidate.rationale: Running out of lives is the moment a player stops. One life keeps them playing without touching the gold-bar sale for a full set of lives, and it costs the game nothing to give.
